title.current: Controlling Owners, Disclosed Intentions, and Minority Shareholder Returns in Korean Captive Spin-Offs

outcome.name: Disposal of the carved-out subsidiary
outcome.conceptual_definition: The event through which the value of the carved-out assets leaves the parent's minority shareholders: after a captive spin-off the parent (controlled by its controlling owner, without a shareholder vote) sells a majority of the new company, lists it, or admits an outside investor; Kang & Lee (2025) show the minority's loss is concentrated in these events.
conceptual_sources: Kang & Lee (2025), Finance Research Letters 85:107826, Section 4 (mechanism paragraph) and footnote 18 (364 of 525 disposed)
Young, Peng, Ahlstrom, Bruton & Jiang (2008), JMS 45(1): principal-principal conflict

operational_definition.unit: carve-out event (parent x newly created company, dated by the receipt date of the original division filing)
operational_definition.positive_rule: disposed = the parent's stake in the new company falls below 50% or the company leaves the parent's equity-investment schedule after appearing (majority_disposed), OR the new company appears in KIND listing records after the division date (ipo_listed), OR the stake falls below 99.5% but stays >= 50% without a listing (partial_sale)
operational_definition.negative_meaning: retained_100 = the parent reports ~100% of the new company in every available annual/half-year report through the latest one read (to fiscal 2025); absence of a qualifying observation, not proof that no disposal will ever occur
operational_definition.time_rule: annual and half-year reports for fiscal years division_year .. min(division_year + 6, 2025); first_change_fy records the first fiscal year showing a change; events too recent to have a record are excluded (unresolved)
operational_definition.data_source: DART Open API DS002 otrCprInvstmntSttus (equity investments in other corporations) and annual-report documents (document.xml) for 2017+ (accessed 2026-10-14 to 10-19); annual-report passages read by Claude (code/09b) for queued 2017+ events and all 2001-2016 events (2026-10-17 to 10-19); KIND listing records
fields: subsidiary tables and division-related passages of the annual report (text)
operational_definition.exclusions: merged back into the parent; liquidated; division cancelled; unmatched/unresolved; too recent (72 + 105 of 758 events)
operational_definition.limitations: 11 of 294 2017-2026 labels are sensitive to the definition or to a conflict between the equity-investment schedule and the annual-report text (intragroup transfer, temporary external dilution, related-party preferred shares, dilution below materiality, source conflict, one tracker mismatch); sensitivity reported in SI Table S1 (flipping all 11 to retained strengthens the headline results). Intent is not observed; only ownership changes are.
sources: DART Open API developer guide, DS002 field definitions
Kang & Lee (2025) Section 4 for the disposed/retained split

concepts.name: Captive spin-off
concepts.definition: A corporate division under the Korean Commercial Act's division provisions in which the surviving company holds 100% of the newly created company (Kang & Lee, 2025, Section 2); unlike a US spin-off no shares are distributed to the parent's shareholders and unlike an equity carve-out no shares are sold or listed at the division.

sources.name: Kang & Lee (2025), Finance Research Letters 85:107826, Section 2 and footnote 6
DART division-resolution filings (hoesa bunhal gyeoljeong; from 2017 the material-event report cmpDvDecsn), division-type field and filing text
Author rule: captive and mixed captive-equity divisions kept; equity spin-offs excluded (code/01, 12b, 12c)

concepts.name: Disposal
concepts.definition: The event through which the value of the carved-out assets leaves the parent's minority shareholders (Kang & Lee, 2025, Section 4): the parent sells a majority of the new company, lists it, or lets its stake fall below 99.5% through a sale or third-party investment. Negative (retained) means 100% is reported through the latest available report.

sources.name: Kang & Lee (2025), Section 4 (disposed vs retained)
DART DS002 equity-investment schedule (otrCprInvstmntSttus: inv_prm, bsis/trmend_blce_qota_rt), half-year reports, KIND listing records
Author rule 99.5% / majority / listed; annual-report passages read by a language model with verbatim evidence (code/02b, 09a-09c, 12d)

concepts.name: Early disposal
concepts.definition: A disposal whose first recorded ownership change falls in the fiscal year of the division or the next (first_change_fy minus division year <= 1), i.e. inside the one-year return window.

sources.name: Author rule on the annual-report labels (code/19_bhar_controls.py)

concepts.name: Disposal signal
concepts.definition: What a careful reader could infer about the controlling owner's intention from the filing alone at the announcement: each of two language models reads the division filing as of its date and returns the probability (0-100) that the parent will not retain 100% of the new company within roughly three to five fiscal years; mean over runs per model, then the two-model mean, rescaled to 0-1.

sources.name: Kang & Lee (2025), Section 4: investors unlikely to discern the intention (the claim tested)
code/04_llm_judge.py prompt and parser; Anthropic claude-fable-5-1 and OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol via a cloud inference service, October 2026

concepts.name: Anonymized condition
concepts.definition: A reading in which recall of the named company's later history is unavailable to the model: parent and new-company names, group names, years and dates masked by regular expressions and the board date withheld (Glasserman & Lin, 2024, for the look-ahead concern).

sources.name: Glasserman & Lin (2024), Journal of Financial Data Science 6(1)
code/04_llm_judge.py anonymize()

concepts.name: Controlling block
concepts.definition: The controlling owner's cash-flow stake in the parent (Young et al., 2008): common shares held by the largest shareholder and the related parties listed with it, excluding treasury shares, at the fiscal year-end before the announcement year; 2016+ from the DART largest-shareholder table (hyslrSttus), earlier from the same table in the annual report read by two models that must agree within 1 percentage point.

sources.name: Young, Peng, Ahlstrom, Bruton & Jiang (2008), Journal of Management Studies 45(1)
DART DS002 hyslrSttus; annual-report largest-shareholder tables (code/20, 20b, 20c)

concepts.name: Announcement CAR
concepts.definition: The immediate price reaction to the filing: market-model cumulative abnormal return over trading days -1 to +1, model estimated on days -250 to -31 against the parent's market index (KOSPI or KOSDAQ); day 0 is the first trading day on or after the receipt date of the original filing.

sources.name: Standard event-study practice; Kang & Lee (2025) Table 1 for the same window

concepts.name: One-year BHAR
concepts.definition: The return to a minority holder who kept the shares after the announcement reaction: buy-and-hold return of the parent minus its market index over trading days +2 to +250; windows with fewer than 90% of trading days dropped; KRX adjusted prices (2017-2026) and Compustat Global daily security file (2001-2016).

sources.name: Barber & Lyon (1997); Lyon, Barber & Tsai (1999); Kang & Lee (2025) Table 1 Panel B

concepts.name: Within-year rank
concepts.definition: The parent's percentile rank (0-1) of the one-year BHAR within its announcement year; a skew-robust ordering within the same calendar environment.

sources.name: Author rule (code/19_bhar_controls.py)

concepts.name: Post-reform period
concepts.definition: Filings received on or after 1 October 2022, i.e. written under the revised disclosure form that requires the division's purpose, expected effects and shareholder-protection measures (FSC press releases of 5 September and 20 December 2022; form applied from 18 October 2022).

sources.name: Financial Services Commission press releases fsc.go.kr/no010101/78449 and /79125
Author cutoff 2022-10-01 (code/23_regulation_2022.py)
